description:
We are a group of STEM students—three in physics and one in computer engineering.

We are interested in science, technological advancements and related projects, both to learn and to contribute.
summary: In this project, we have developed a "survival guide" for Mars. It is an interactive web map of the Jezero crater, designed to facilitate future missions. To address this challenge, we have analyzed data sourced from NASA and the USGS. This enabled us to create an interface that allows for the overlay of various layers—such as elevation, solar radiation, rockiness, and more. It serves as an intuitive visual tool of great importance for future missions, as it helps identify safe zones and potential biosignatures—but, above all, it ensures that astronauts remain safe and can successfully complete their mission.
details: The system displays a hyper-localized map featuring various layers designed to help astronauts navigate and stay safe. Users can select areas of interest to generate the safest and most efficient routes, optimized based on specific priorities—such as travel time, oxygen reserves, metabolic energy expenditure, battery life, or radiation exposure. Furthermore, users can toggle different layers to visualize terrain features—including rock outcrops, geological maps, river delta fans, carbonate deposits, dunes and sand, volcanic substrates, or even solar radiation levels (a particularly innovative feature). This is especially significant, as it allows astronauts to familiarize themselves with specific terrain—such as the Jezero Crater—in advance, thereby facilitating mission operations. To develop this project, we utilized AI and programming languages ​​including Python, JavaScript, and CSS.
